description: The pie chart represents the distribution of various news sources, comparing their relative proportions. The chart is divided into 17 slices, each representing a different news source. The slices are labeled with the name of the news source and are colored differently, although some colors are similar and not easily distinguishable. The proportions of the slices are as follows: Breitbart (blue) at approximately 14%, Other (gray) at around 11%, Drudge Report (orange) and The Daily Caller (green) both at about 8%, The Huffington Post (red) at 7%, NPR (purple) and Vox (brown) both at 6%, The Guardian (pink) and BBC (brown) both at 5%, and the remaining sources - RT (teal), Daily Kos (yellow), National Review (blue), Daily Mail (orange), Red State (red), Fox News (red), CNN (light blue), PoliticusUSA (pink), and Shareblue (purple) - each at 3%. The chart includes numerical labels inside each slice, indicating their respective percentages. The slices are arranged in a seemingly unordered manner, with no apparent visual emphasis on any particular slice.
